title: Finding Side a of a Triangle Using the Law of Sines
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A triangle has side c = 2 and angles A = \pi/4 and B = \pi/3. Find the length a of the side opposite angle A.

steps.title: Find the Third Angle C
steps.explanation: Use the triangle angle-sum theorem A + B + C = pi to find C = 5*pi/12.
steps.why: The interior angles of any Euclidean triangle sum to pi radians (180 degrees).

steps.title: Apply the Law of Sines to Solve for a
steps.explanation: Express side a in terms of c = 2, sin(pi/4), and sin(5*pi/12).
steps.why: By the Law of Sines, a/sin A = c/sin C.

steps.title: Substitute Exact Radical Values and Simplify
steps.explanation: Substitute sin(pi/4) = sqrt(2)/2 and sin(5*pi/12) = (sqrt(6) + sqrt(2))/4 (from Exercise 46), cancel sqrt(2), and rationalize the denominator by multiplying by (sqrt(3) - 1)/(sqrt(3) - 1).
